ft-1782182999139-2340.why: The Bitdeer article describes 'Bitdeer's plan for a 15-building campus of up to 750 megawatts on about 257 acres at the Turnpike Commerce Center' in Shalersville, and the record's own first source is headlined 'Bitdeer looks to develop 750MW data center campus in Ohio'. 150 MW appears nowhere. Status 'proposed' is right: 'In Portage County, nothing has been approved'.

ft-1767584334287-8832.name: Atlas Data Center (South Whitehall)
ft-1767584334287-8832.why: The developer field was blank. The Lehigh County article says 'In South Whitehall, CDE Acquisitions has proposed the Atlas Data Center across the road from Parkland High School'. Status 'proposed' is right. The 725 MW comes from a source headlined about Edged; the article gives no megawatt figure, so capacity is left for the merge to judge.

ft-1779304944409-7202.why: The developer field was blank. The Davidson County article says Fisk University 'announced in May a campus master plan that includes a 100,000-square-foot innovation and technology center with a 30-megawatt data center', with Don Hardin's firm managing it. Status 'proposed' and 30 MW match.

ft-526.why: The Ector County article says the project 'was first pitched at 90MW before being enlarged to 250MW', and that in September 2026 New Era signed for 'at least 207MW for the first phase'; its CEO said the company 'now had the land, construction permits and contracted power', with no construction reported. 1,000 MW appears nowhere. Permitted but not building = approved. The developer field was blank; the article names New Era Energy & Digital, which bought out Sharon AI's half.

ft-1783826724382-4737.why: The Angelina County article says 'HyperDataGrid ... is developing a data center on the former Northern Chip Mill site on Ben Dunn Road off Highway 103 West; Wright said it had secured power and water agreements and begun clearing land.' Site clearing under way with no approval still needed: under construction. The developer field was blank. NOTE for the merge: this Lufkin, Texas record is also printed on the Labette County, Kansas page, whose article is about a separate HyperDatagrid option in Parsons.

ft-1786992679173-8336.why: The developer field was blank. The Bowie County article says 'Potentia Development plans a 500-acre campus there' at TexAmericas Center, Project Big Pine. Status 'proposed' is right. The article gives no megawatt figure, so the 300 MW is left for the merge to judge.

ft-611.name: Sulphur Springs Matrix Data Center Campus
ft-611.why: The Hopkins County article says 'By July ... the mayor announced that MSB Global would no longer lead the development; no replacement has been named', and a court injunction bars the on-site power the plan relied on, with trial not expected until November 2027. So MSB Global is no longer the developer and the name should not carry its brand. Status left 'proposed'; the 3,000 MW is not in the article and is left for the merge to judge.

ft-1784074174322-9081.why: The Hopewell article says the 20 MW figure comes from a consultant's case study that the city says it 'did not commission, participate in, or conduct', that the study 'had been taken down', and that 'No application has been reported.' No one has proposed anything to the city, so 'proposed (early)' overstates it.

ft-1109.why: The 2,398 MW belongs to the power plant, not the data centre: the Mingo County article says each gas plant 'would be able to generate more than 2,400 megawatts' according to the air permit applications, and gives no data centre load. The state 'granted air permits for both power plants in October 2025' and a federal judge refused to halt the project, so it is past 'proposed'. The article names the company 'TransGas Development Systems'.

epoch-openai-stargate-michigan.why: The Washtenaw County article says 'the developer Related Digital and the landowners sued' and a consent judgment allowed 'a $7 billion Oracle and OpenAI project to proceed'; the Oracle article says 'on most of its sites Oracle is the tenant and cloud operator, with OpenAI as its customer', naming 'Related Digital's campus in Saline Township', and calls it 'the 1.4-gigawatt campus'. Status 'under construction' is right: a judge refused 'a request to slow construction'.

blocked-delaware-city-project-washington.why: The New Castle County article says Project Washington would have drawn '1.2 gigawatts'. Status 'blocked' is right: the Environmental Secretary ruled it barred by the Coastal Zone Act and the Coastal Zone Industrial Control Board unanimously upheld that; Starwood then withdrew its court appeal.

blocked-salem-mill-creek-corporate-cente.why: Same project as ft-1784230987783-1009 ('Verrus Data Center', Deer Park Dr SE and Turner Rd SE, Salem). The Marion County article describes one Verrus campus at the Mill Creek Corporate Center, and lane d has corrected that record to 'proposed' with developer Verrus. This record's 'blocked' is also wrong: the governor cancelled the sale of 32 state acres, but Verrus 'is looking at an adjacent 32-acre parcel' and 'filed its first application' on July 31. Keep ft-1784230987783-1009, which has the more specific address.

ft-1764303051982-5528.why: The Coconino County article says 'City documents say the buyer intends to seek permits for a 1-gigawatt data center campus'. Status 'proposed' is right: the land sale waits on an 18-to-24-month feasibility study.

ft-1786764095148-3335.why: The New Castle County article says the project that 'would redevelop the White Clay Center office park east of Newark' was 'recently paused' by its developers after Councilman Tim Sheldon 'brokered an informal deal with them'. The record's address is the terminus of White Clay Center Drive.

ft-1771258984530-9087.why: The record's own sources are headlined '$2 billion data center proposal in Barrington Hills withdrawn' (Northwest Herald, January 29, 2026) and 'Brennan Investment Group withdraws plans for $2bn data center outside Chicago'. The developer withdrew it, and the developer field was blank. The Cook County article does not mention it.

ft-256.why: The developer field was blank; the record's name is 'Karis Critical Data Center' and its sources are about Merrillville, Indiana. Status left 'proposed'. The Lake County article says Merrillville put a moratorium in place from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 after four developers approached it. NOTE for the merge: this Crown Point/Merrillville, Indiana record is also printed on the DeKalb County and DuPage County, Illinois pages. That is how a 'Karis ... PROPOSED' row turns up beside the DuPage article that says Naperville rejected Karis; it is a filing error.

ft-279.why: The St. Joseph County article says the $12 billion, roughly 1,000-acre proposal off Chicago Trail east of New Carlisle 'did not survive': the Area Plan Commission sent it to the council unfavorably 7-0, and 'the St. Joseph County Council voted 7-2 against the rezoning in December 2025'. A rezoning denied by the deciding body is blocked, not suspended. The article notes the developer may bring it back after six months.

ft-1766087804541-4477.why: The Androscoggin County article says 'The council voted unanimously against the project' on Dec. 16, 2025, and the record's own sources are headlined 'Lewiston city council shoots down data center proposal' and 'Lewiston city councilors unanimously vote down AI data center proposal'. Voted down by the deciding body = blocked. The developer did not withdraw; nobody from MillCompute spoke.

ft-311.why: The St. Louis County article says 'On 20 October 2025 ... the city council approved the rezoning', that 'the developer, Mortenson' held the NDAs, and that 'On 3 March 2026 Google said it was the company', with a Minnesota Power agreement in place. The city is redoing its environmental review and a lawsuit is pending, but nothing says the project is suspended. Rezoned = approved.

ft-331.why: The developer field was blank; the record is DartPoints' Asheville facility and its source is DartPoints' own North Carolina page. NOTE for the merge: this Asheville record is also printed on the Bartholomew County, Indiana page, whose article describes a different DartPoints building in Columbus, Indiana, and on the Caddo Parish, Louisiana page. Both are filing errors; it belongs only on Buncombe County.

ft-1772681077912-7681.why: The developer field was blank. The Buffalo County article describes 'a 40,000-square-foot Sequitor Edge edge data center planned at Tech oNE Crossing for 2027', which confirms 'proposed'. NOTE for the merge: this Kearney, Nebraska record is also printed on the Pennington County, South Dakota page, which is about a separate Sequitor Edge project in Rapid City.

ft-1768320725363-3199.name: Strata Expanse AI Data Center (Hanging Rock)
ft-1768320725363-3199.why: The Lawrence County article says 'In December 2025 Strata Expanse ... held a ribbon-cutting for an AI data center at 1476 County Road 1A near Hanging Rock, in Hamilton Township, with RAVEL and Supermicro as tenants'. A ribbon-cutting marks an opened facility, so 'proposed' contradicts the article. The developer is 'Strata Expanse', not 'Strata', and RAVEL is a tenant, not the project's name. NOTE: the address says Ironton, but the article says the site is in Hamilton Township and 'Ironton has no say over the site'.

ft-459.why: The same Fox 43 URL was listed twice, so the page shows a duplicate source link. I removed the duplicate. Nothing else changed; the Dauphin County article does not mention the Dauphin Highlands golf course project.

ft-1770776013460-3256.why: The Montour County article says 'In February 2026 the three commissioners unanimously denied rezoning more than 800 acres', and the record's own sources are headlined 'Proposal for 800-acre data center in central Pennsylvania has been denied' and 'Local regulators deny rezoning request'. Denied by the deciding body = blocked, not suspended. Talen says it is still 'committed to pursuing a path forward', which the note does not change.

ft-1786570153211-1394.why: The record's own source is headlined 'Unnamed developer withdraws data center in Brownsville, Texas'. The Cameron County article describes the request to use 'the old Southwest Key Casa Padre building, a former Walmart' (the record's address) and the outcry against it. The developer withdrew; nothing was cancelled after approval.

ft-1777471887054-2686.name: ONMINE Data Center
ft-1777471887054-2686.why: The Bell County article says 'the Planning and Zoning Commission voted 4-1 in April 2026 against ONMINE's $30 million "computing and energy research annex"' and that 'The applicant withdrew before the June 2 council vote.' The commission only recommends, so the final act was the applicant's withdrawal, not a block. The article spells the company ONMINE.

ft-888.name: Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation
ft-888.why: Spelling: 'Grummon' in the name; the record's own developer field and the company are 'Northrop Grumman'.

ft-1769230835913-8005.why: The Caroline County article says supervisors 'rejected the plan amendment 5-1' on June 18, 2024 for VALCO's 900-acre campus on Mount Airy Drive, and then 'VALCO withdrew its rezoning request.' Its only cited source belongs to a different project: its URL is '10m-sq-ft-amazon-files-for-four-data-center-campuses-in-virginias-spotsylvania-and-caroline-counties', Amazon's campuses, including Mattameade. I removed it. The developer field was blank.

ft-1778596114883-8026.why: The Milwaukee County article says that on July 6 'the developer would drop the computing facility', and the revised plan of housing, library and storage was approved without it on July 20. The record's own second source is headlined 'Plans for Milwaukee data center in former Walmart building shelved'. The developer withdrew the data center part. The article names the owner 'AFS Milwaukee LLC, led by ... Trent Overhue'.
